design:
D1 Inside the gate's savepoint. The acceptances are written in a nested transaction that also runs the gate, so a refused approval leaves nothing accepted and the gate reads the accepted state it will merge from. project_checks.schedule keys on the task, so a rollback leaves no dangling check row.
D2 Only the task's own pieces (task_id equal to the task). Another task's piece serving the same requirement is that task's reviewer's to decide; the gate's mixed case already admits approval when something else merges.
D3 The grant stays. decide_evidence and can_accept_evidence still work for pieces outside a review; nothing reads the grant on the verdict path.
D4 Hazard and rollback. This changes what the approval gate admits, so what merges into main: an agent's approval now merges work whose evidence nobody else judged. Mitigation is the operator's overturn (operator-overturns). Rollback is reverting the commit; no migration, no data to undo (the review rows written stay true: they record who decided).

problem: F672: on Terra a reviewer judged the work right, its approval was refused because 10 evidence pieces awaited a decision only the operator or a granted agent could make, the loop skipped with that sentence as the only record, and granting the right afterwards did not re-run the reviewer. Evidence is decided by a separate grant (agents.can_accept_evidence, requirement_evidence.may_accept) that nobody had given, while the reviewer already judges the same work. The operator decided (vis-D1, vis-D4, 2026-10-17) to remove themselves from evidence judgment: the reviewing agent's verdict decides the task's evidence. Tier 2: it changes what the approval gate admits and so what merges into main.

requirements.rationale: The reviewer has judged the work the evidence demonstrates; a second decision by someone else is what stalled Terra.
requirements.statement: When a task moves to approved, every piece of evidence recorded for that task that is still awaiting MUST be accepted by the approving actor in the same transaction, its review reason being the verdict's notes or, without notes, a sentence naming the approval, except a piece the approving agent recorded itself or whose recording run is still live.
When the approval is refused for any reason, no acceptance made for it MUST persist, and the refusal MUST name the real reason rather than the evidence it would have accepted.

requirements.rationale: A rejection is the author's signal of what to fix.
requirements.statement: When a task moves to revision_needed or rejected, every awaiting piece of evidence recorded for that task MUST be rejected by the acting actor, its reason being the verdict's notes or, without notes, a sentence naming the verdict, except a piece the acting agent recorded itself or whose recording run is still live.

An approval MUST NOT be held for the operator, and a review briefing MUST NOT tell the reviewer that deciding evidence is the operator's, because of evidence recorded for the task under review; the briefing MUST say that the verdict decides that evidence.

requirements.rationale: The operator leaves the gate but keeps the last word.
requirements.statement: When the operator rejects an accepted piece of evidence whose task is approved, the task MUST move to revision_needed with the operator as actor.

in_scope: apply_transition: a move to approved accepts the task's own awaiting evidence inside the gate's savepoint; a move to revision_needed or rejected rejects it
approval_held_for_operator and the review briefing stop treating the task's own awaiting evidence as the operator's
The operator rejecting an accepted piece of an approved task reopens the task
non_goals: Removing the can_accept_evidence grant or decide_evidence (still usable for evidence outside a review)
Evidence recorded by another task serving the same requirement (that task's verdict decides it)

summary: Approving a task accepts the evidence it recorded and sending it back rejects it, so evidence never waits on the operator and a loop never stalls on it.
